messages.settings.title: Settings
messages.settings.notice.plaintext: Settings are kept in this browser in plain text, including RPC URLs. Do not put a URL there that contains a secret you would not store in plain text. No key is ever stored.
messages.settings.rpc.hint: Only https:// and wss:// are accepted, with no username or password. The chain id is verified when the endpoint is used. No default RPC is built in.
messages.settings.rpc.connected: Connected. The endpoint reports the expected chain id.
messages.settings.rpc.failed: Failed: the endpoint is unreachable or reports a different chain.
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.label: {chain} second RPC URL (optional)
messages.settings.rpc.secondary.hint: A different provider. Scans compare it with the main RPC and withhold the checkpoint when they disagree.
messages.settings.relayer.label: Relayer URL (optional)
messages.settings.relayer.hint: https only. The relayer sees the one-time address, destination, token, amount and timing of each sweep it handles.
messages.settings.delay.range: Each payment is delayed between {min, number} and {max, number} seconds.
messages.settings.lock.idleLabel: Idle lock after minutes without activity
messages.settings.lock.keysHint: After this many minutes without a click or key press, local tags lock. Seller keys are wiped from memory at the same time only when a copy survives the wipe: keys you imported (for hex keys imported without their signing key, the signing key generated here is lost), keys whose keystore you downloaded, or keys whose vault is still saved in this browser. Keys with no backup stay loaded, with a warning, until you back them up, wipe them or close the tab.
messages.settings.lock.summary: Locks after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity.

messages.settings.storageUnavailable: Browser storage is unavailable, so these settings apply to this tab only.

messages.settings.error.lock: Lock timeout must be 1 to 240 minutes.

messages.sweep.title: Sweep
messages.sweep.choosePayment: Choose a payment to sweep from Scan and receive.
messages.sweep.keysGone: Your keys are no longer in memory. Load them again in Seller keys.
messages.sweep.vaultCancelledKeys: Vault check cancelled because seller keys changed.
messages.sweep.paymentsDisabledChain: Payments are disabled on this chain: no deployment manifest is loaded.
messages.sweep.balanceUnknown: unknown (an RPC for this chain is required)
messages.sweep.noManifest: Payments disabled on this chain: no deployment manifest is loaded.
messages.sweep.tokenNotAllowed: This token is not on the allowlist. It will not be swept from here.
messages.sweep.payerFollow.title: The payer can follow this sweep
messages.sweep.payerFollow.body: The payer knows the one-time address. When you move its funds, the destination and everything else that address has received or will receive are public and linkable. Use a fresh destination for each sweep, and avoid an address already known to be yours if you do not want to link those funds. A relayer also sees your IP address (hashed), amount and timing. Your stealth key is derived in memory for this action and is never shown or stored.
messages.sweep.destination.label: Destination address (your own wallet)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.label: Vault passphrase (required for each sweep action)
messages.sweep.vaultPass.hint: Checked against the encrypted vault that holds the seller keys loaded now: the one they were unlocked from, saved to or found in, which stays in memory for this session even if the saved vault is deleted. It is cleared after every action. Do not let your browser save it.
messages.sweep.vaultError: Could not check encrypted vault storage, so sweep signing is disabled until storage is available.
messages.sweep.feeLegend: How to pay the network fee
messages.sweep.modeRelayer: Through the relayer (fee deducted from the amount; needs a permit-capable token)
messages.sweep.modeDirect: Directly (the one-time address must hold native coin for gas)
messages.sweep.relayerNeeds: Relayer sweeps need a relayer URL in Settings and a token with ERC-2612 permit. Use a direct sweep otherwise.
messages.sweep.checkExplorer: Check it on your RPC or a block explorer you trust before relying on it.
messages.sweep.pendingBlocksSigning: A sweep from this address may still be pending. Check its status before signing anything new.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownDirect: The signed transaction was handed to your RPC but its result is unknown. It may already be on the network, so a new sweep is disabled. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce and retains every earlier transaction hash.
messages.sweep.attempt.unknownRelayed: The signed order was handed to the relayer but its result is unknown. It can still execute until {deadline}; it counts as expired only {minutes} minutes after that. Signing a new one is disabled until then.
messages.sweep.attempt.expiredBody: The order's nonce was still unused after its deadline, so it can no longer execute and moved nothing. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.refusedBody: The relayer reported that it refused the order before sending it. This relies on the relayer's report; the signed order stays valid until {deadline}. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.attempt.replacedBody: No receipt was found for this hash or for any earlier attempt with the same nonce, but that nonce is already used in a finalized block, so this transaction can never be included. Another transaction with that nonce (for example one signed in another tab) was included instead. Check the address on a block explorer. You can sign again.
messages.sweep.permit.ok: The permit checks passed: the token will accept this signature for exactly the sweep amount.
messages.sweep.permit.alreadyAllowed: An allowance already covers this sweep, so the permit is skipped and the sweep uses the allowance. Nothing else is needed.
messages.sweep.permit.nonceConsumed: This permit was already used or replaced (its nonce is spent) and no allowance covers the sweep. Nothing was moved. It will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.failed: The relayer reported that the token rejected the permit (invalid signature or a permit that was already used), so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.expired: The relayer reported that the permit had already expired, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.unsupported: The relayer reported that this token does not accept standard ERC-2612 permits, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and nothing will be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.valueTooLow: The relayer reported that the signed permit did not cover the full amount, so it refused the order before sending it. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Sign a new sweep.
messages.sweep.permit.noAllowance: The relayer reported that the stealth address has no allowance and no usable permit, so it refused the order. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically.
messages.sweep.permit.ownerFailureLimit: The relayer refused this order because there were too many failed sweep attempts from this address in the last hour. Nothing was moved and it will not be retried automatically. Wait before signing again.
messages.sweep.permit.directFallback: You can sweep directly instead: the stealth address then pays the network fee itself and needs a little native coin for gas.
messages.sweep.note.pendingRelayed: The order has not executed yet, and no finalized block is far enough past its deadline to treat it as expired. It may still execute; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.pendingDirect: No receipt found for this hash yet. That does not mean it was not sent; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.noRpc: No RPC is configured for this chain, so the status was not checked. The outcome is still unknown.
messages.sweep.note.checkFailed: The status check failed. The outcome is still unknown; check again later.
messages.sweep.note.lockChanged: This sweep's record changed while the status was being checked, so the result was not applied. Check again.
messages.sweep.resign.hint: Use this only if the network most likely never accepted this transaction (your RPC failed at handoff or no longer reports any recorded transaction). The replacement goes to the destination entered above with the same nonce {nonce}, so at most one of them can ever be included; Check status looks for each of them. It is not a fee bump, so it does not speed up a transaction the network already holds.
messages.sweep.resign.limit: Replacement limit reached. Check the recorded transactions until their outcome is resolved; signing stays locked.
messages.sweep.note.rpcForgot: The configured RPC no longer reports any recorded transaction. This does not prove they were dropped everywhere. When available below, a replacement uses the same nonce; a new sweep stays locked.
messages.sweep.resign.button: Sign a replacement with the same nonce
messages.sweep.resign.nothingPending: There is no pending direct sweep to replace. Check its status.
messages.sweep.dryRunUnavailable: Your RPC could not dry-run this sweep, so it was signed and sent without that check. Check the transaction on a block explorer.
messages.sweep.journalBroken.title: Signing disabled in this tab
messages.sweep.journalBroken.body: The sweep attempt record in this tab is unavailable or invalid. Signing stays disarmed; a sweep may still be pending. Check the address on a block explorer before trying again in a new tab.

messages.sellerKeys.keystoreDownloaded: Encrypted keystore downloaded. Keep the file and remember the passphrase: neither can be recovered.
messages.sellerKeys.notKeystore: This is not a GhostPay keystore file.
messages.sellerKeys.keystoreDecrypted: Keystore decrypted; keys are in memory.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultSaved: Encrypted seller vault saved in this browser. The passphrase was cleared.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultUnlocked: Encrypted vault unlocked. Seller keys are back in memory.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultDeleted: Encrypted vault deleted from this browser.
messages.sellerKeys.keystoreReceived: Encrypted keystore received. Enter its passphrase and choose Decrypt and load.
messages.sellerKeys.title: Seller keys
messages.sellerKeys.memory.title: Keys stay in memory by default
messages.sellerKeys.memory.body: Keys are generated and used only inside this page. They are never written to browser storage unless you explicitly save the optional encrypted vault below. Reloading or closing the tab forgets keys that were not saved. The idle lock in Settings also wipes keys from memory, but only keys that can be loaded again: imported (from hex keys without their signing key, the signing key generated here is lost), downloaded as a keystore or saved in the vault.
messages.sellerKeys.checkingVault: Checking for an encrypted seller vault…
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.title: Encrypted browser storage is unavailable
messages.sellerKeys.storageUnavailable.body: This browser cannot read the optional vault. In-memory key use and encrypted file backups remain available, but do not try to save a local vault here.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultSavedHeading: Encrypted seller vault saved in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.unlockExplain: Unlocking replaces the keys currently in memory. The vault stores only the encrypted keystore text; GhostPay never stores your passphrase.
messages.sellerKeys.vaultNoBrowserSave: Do not let your browser or password manager save this passphrase, even when it offers to: anyone using this browser profile could then unlock the vault, which defeats the vault and the idle lock.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteExplain: This permanently deletes the saved ciphertext in this browser. Keep a separate backup first if needed.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteHolds: This vault holds the seller keys of meta-address:
messages.sellerKeys.deleteLoaded: These are the keys loaded now. Enter this vault’s passphrase to delete it.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteOther: These are not the keys loaded now.
messages.sellerKeys.deleteUnreadable: This record is not a valid keystore, so its meta-address cannot be shown.
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplaces.title: The keys loaded now have no backup
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplaces.body: Unlocking the saved vault replaces them, and every payment sent to their meta-address can then never be swept. Back them up first unless you are sure they hold nothing.
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplacesSignerOnly.titl: The signing key loaded now has no backup
messages.sellerKeys.unlockReplacesSignerOnly.body: Unlocking the saved vault replaces the loaded keys. Payments to their meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but the invoice-signing key generated here is lost: nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed. Back the keys up first unless you do not need that key.
messages.sellerKeys.stepUp.label: Passphrase of the vault these keys are tied to
messages.sellerKeys.stepUp.hint: These keys were unlocked from, saved to or found in an encrypted vault in this browser, so that vault’s passphrase is needed before they are exported or saved under a new passphrase, even if the vault has been deleted since.
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.label: Invoice-signing private key (optional)
messages.sellerKeys.signKey.hint: Leave empty to generate a new signing key here. It exists only in this tab until you download the encrypted keystore or save the vault: if the tab closes or the idle lock wipes the keys before then, your hex keys load the spending and viewing keys again, but with a new signing key. It must not be your spending or viewing key.
messages.sellerKeys.metaShare: Share this to receive payments. It reveals no private key.
messages.sellerKeys.payersSee: “signature matches key …”. They can pin this key; an unpinned key identifies nobody.
messages.sellerKeys.suggested: Suggested: {words} random words picked on this device ({bits} bits). Write it down, then type it again below, or replace it with your own.
messages.sellerKeys.formatNote: Format: scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and AES-256-GCM. GhostPay does not store the passphrase anywhere.
messages.sellerKeys.forgetQr: Forget encrypted QR from this page
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExplain: This keeps an encrypted keystore in this browser’s IndexedDB so you can unlock after reload. Anyone with access to this browser profile can copy the ciphertext and attempt offline guesses; choose a strong passphrase. Browser storage can be cleared or lost, so keep a separate backup. GhostPay never saves the passphrase or plaintext key material here.
messages.sellerKeys.saveVault: Save encrypted vault in this browser
messages.sellerKeys.vaultExists: A vault already exists. It is never overwritten automatically; unlock or explicitly delete it before saving a different key set.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeUnsaved.title: Wipe keys that have no backup?
messages.sellerKeys.wipeUnsaved.body: No copy of these keys exists outside this tab. Wiping them loses them for good, and every payment sent to their meta-address can then never be swept. Back them up first unless you are sure they hold nothing.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeSignerOnly.title: Wipe keys whose signing key has no backup?
messages.sellerKeys.wipeSignerOnly.body: Payments to their meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but the invoice-signing key generated here exists only in this tab. Once it is wiped, nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed. Back the keys up first unless you do not need that key.
messages.sellerKeys.wipeHint: This removes the keys from this tab only. Scan checkpoints, scan history, local tags and any saved vault stay in this browser, and anyone with this browser profile and your meta-address can tell from them that these keys were used here. To remove them, clear this site’s data in your browser settings, after backing up what you need.
messages.sellerKeys.registryHint: Publishing your meta-address to the ERC-6538 registry would publicly associate it with your wallet address. Publishing is optional and has its own page.
messages.backupGate.title: Back up these seller keys first
messages.backupGate.body: Invoices and the meta-address invite payments that only these keys can sweep, and the keys exist only in this tab. If it closes or the browser crashes before you back them up, those payments are lost for good.
messages.backupGate.signerOnly.body: Payments stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported, but invoices are signed with an invoice-signing key that exists only in this tab. If it closes, reloads or crashes, or the idle lock wipes the keys, before you back them up, nothing can be signed with that key again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed.
messages.backupGate.waiverLabel: To continue without a backup, type: {phrase}
messages.app.backup.title: These seller keys have no backup
messages.app.backup.body: They exist only in this tab. If it closes, reloads or crashes before you back them up, every payment sent to their meta-address is lost. Until then the idle lock leaves them loaded.
messages.app.backup.signerOnly.title: The invoice-signing key has no backup
messages.app.backup.signerOnly.body: Payments to your meta-address stay sweepable with the spending and viewing keys you imported. The invoice-signing key was generated in this tab and exists nowhere else: once the tab closes, reloads or crashes, or the idle lock wipes the keys, nothing can be signed with it again, not even receipts for the invoices it signed.
messages.app.idle.wiped: Seller keys wiped from memory and local tags locked after inactivity.
messages.app.idle.kept: Local tags locked after inactivity. Seller keys stay loaded because they have no backup yet.
messages.app.idle.wipedNotice: Seller keys were wiped from memory after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without activity. Load them again under Seller keys from your keystore file, the browser vault or your hex keys.
messages.app.idle.signerLost: The invoice-signing key generated when the hex keys were imported had no backup and is gone: loading them again generates a new one.
messages.settings.outside.title: Settings can be changed outside this page
messages.settings.outside.body: Anything that can write to this site’s browser storage, including another local user, malware or an extension, can change these RPC, relayer and pinned-signer settings. Review the endpoints and signer keys before relying on them. A second RPC can reveal disagreements, but it does not make either provider trustworthy by itself.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errWindow: Window size must be a whole number of blocks from 0 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errDelays: Delays must be whole milliseconds, minimum at most maximum, up to 10000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.errBudget: The per-scan budget must be from 1 to 100000.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.saved: Scan privacy settings saved. They apply to the next scan.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.refused: This browser refused to store the scan privacy settings.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.hint: These options change how announcements are fetched, not what is on-chain. A web page cannot open a SOCKS connection or check that it runs in Tor Browser: “Tor Browser” means you opened this page in Tor Browser yourself; “Local proxy” means a JSON-RPC forwarder you run on this computer (for example one that sends traffic over Tor). Defaults add no new destination.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.requireProxy: Require the private path (block the scan instead of falling back; skip the direct second RPC behind a local proxy)
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointRequired: Required: an address on 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.endpointOptional: Optional: leave empty to use the RPC above.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.sourceIndexer: Public-log indexer (block hashes checked against your RPC)
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.windowHint: Everyone using the same window sends identical range queries. Capped at the chain's log range.
messages.settings.scanPrivacy.budgetHint: Announcements posted by the GhostPay router are always checked first. Others beyond this budget are deferred to the next scan, never skipped.

messages.home.release.label: SHA-256 of the app script you are running:
messages.home.release.compare: Compare it with the hash the maintainers publish for this release. A host that serves different files to different visitors is not detected by this check.
messages.about.title: About and privacy
messages.about.intro: GhostPay creates one-time (stealth) addresses so that a seller’s receiving address is not published. It is a static page: there is no GhostPay server, account or analytics, and it loads no third-party code or fonts.
messages.about.feeNote: Gas-sponsored sweeps charge max(110 % of the gas cost, 0.5 % of the amount), capped at 3 %, shown in the quote before you sign. The optional gas buffer and the delay are free.
messages.about.verify.title: How to verify this release
messages.about.verify.intro: The SHA-256 on Home is informational: this page computes it from a script fetched from the same host. A compromised host could serve both the app and the hash it wants you to see, so that check does not establish that the release is authentic.
messages.about.verify.step1: Download the published release and its checksum from a second channel, then verify the files locally with the published SHA256SUMS.
messages.about.verify.step2: When a release key is built into this app, the deployment manifest must have a valid signature from one of those keys. That signature only helps if you have verified the app bundle itself.
messages.about.verify.step3: Check that the deployment addresses and code match the chain through an RPC you trust. A second independent RPC can expose disagreements, but agreement alone does not prove either provider is honest.
messages.about.verify.step4: Before sending, check that the final screen and your wallet show the same contract, one-time address, amounts and fee recipient.
messages.about.verify.step5: Hosting headers such as CSP and Referrer-Policy only apply on hosts that support them; static hosts may not be able to enforce every policy.
messages.about.noAudit: No external audit of this software has been performed.
messages.errorBoundary.title: This page stopped after an unexpected error
messages.errorBoundary.body: Nothing else happens on this page. If a wallet request was open, check your wallet and a block explorer before you try again: a transaction may already have been sent. No error details are shown, because they could contain invoice text.
messages.errorBoundary.reloadHint: Reloading clears everything that is kept only in this tab, including seller keys that are not backed up.
messages.registry.publicAssoc.body: Registering writes your meta-address into a public contract, linked permanently to the wallet address that sends the transaction. Anyone can then see that this wallet receives GhostPay payments and can look up where to pay it. This cannot be undone; you can only overwrite the entry. If that link would harm your privacy, do not publish, and share the meta-address directly instead. Clearing or overwriting replaces the current value but does not erase transaction history.
messages.registry.publicAssoc.title: This is a public association with your wallet address
messages.registry.canonicalTail: , taken from the text of EIP-6538. The page checks that contract code exists on the chosen network and checks its ERC-6538 identity before use. Test networks only until mainnets are enabled.
messages.registry.title: Public registry (ERC-6538)
messages.registry.noRpc: Set an RPC endpoint for this network in Settings first. This page refuses to continue without an independent check.
messages.registry.sessionChanged: The registry session, network, wallet or consent changed. Review the action again.
messages.registry.txChanged: The reviewed registry transaction changed. Review it again.
messages.registry.verified: Your RPC saw the same transaction you reviewed.
messages.registry.notSeen: Your RPC has not seen it yet; check a block explorer.
messages.registry.clearNote: This removes the current entry only; public chain history remains visible.
messages.registry.walletReturned: The wallet returned transaction {hash}. The session changed or verification failed; check your wallet and the journal before another attempt. This request cannot be cancelled or rolled back by this page.
messages.registry.loadKeysFirst: Load or generate keys under Seller keys first.
messages.registry.consent: I understand this publicly associates my meta-address with my wallet address.
messages.registry.qrHint: Scanned text is untrusted. Reading it does not change seller keys or write to the registry. Confirm the owner's identity through another channel.
messages.registry.qrLabel: Scan or paste a public meta-address
messages.registry.lookupLabel: Wallet address (ENS names are not supported yet)
messages.registry.readOnlyHeading: Read-only call (nothing is sent from your wallet)
messages.registry.notRegistered: No meta-address is registered for this address on {chain}.
messages.registry.registeredBy.title: Registered by the owner of that address
messages.registry.registeredBy.body: Only the wallet itself (or a signature from it) can set this entry, but you should still confirm the address with the payee out of band before sending funds.
messages.btc.title: Bitcoin silent payments (test networks)
messages.btc.warning.title: Proof of concept, test networks only
messages.btc.warning.body: Unaudited. Mainnet is disabled. Use only coins that have no value (testnet4, signet or a local regtest node). Keys are held in memory and are never saved; write down the seed if you want to keep the wallet.
messages.btc.network.label: Network
messages.btc.server.label: Esplora server URL
messages.btc.server.hint: Any Esplora-compatible REST server you trust for this network (https, or http to localhost for regtest). It sees every block height you scan, each matching output outpoint you check for spent status, and any transaction you broadcast. It cannot see your keys.
messages.btc.wallet.importHint: 64 hex characters (32 bytes) from a wallet created here. Test coins only.
messages.btc.payment.heading: Payment instructions
messages.btc.payment.step1: Open a wallet that supports BIP-352 silent payments on {network}.
messages.btc.payment.step2: Send to the address above, or scan the QR code or open this link:
messages.btc.payment.step3: Wait for one confirmation, then use "Scan" below starting a few blocks before the payment.
messages.btc.payment.caption: Silent payment request ({network})
messages.btc.seed.warning: Anyone with this seed controls the wallet. It is not stored anywhere.
messages.btc.seed.heading: Backup seed
messages.btc.seed.hiddenHint: It is hidden. Show it only where nobody can see your screen; it hides again after a minute, or as soon as this tab is hidden.
messages.btc.seed.copyWarning: Other apps and web pages can read the clipboard, and it may be kept in a clipboard history or synced to your other devices. Copy only to paste it straight into a password manager. Hide, Lock and leaving this view empty the clipboard again (best effort). When the browser does not allow that at the time (for example when the app locks itself while you are away), it happens at your next click or key press in this page.
messages.btc.seed.copied: Copied. Paste it now: Hide, Lock and leaving this view empty the clipboard again.
messages.btc.seed.copyFailed: Copy failed: select the text manually.
messages.btc.appLocked: The app locked, so this wallet's keys were wiped from memory. Import the backup seed to use it again.
messages.btc.scan.heightHint: Scans at most {max} blocks per run up to the server tip. Whole blocks are downloaded and checked on this device.
messages.btc.scan.details: What the scan checks, and what it does not
messages.btc.scan.checked: Checked on this device for every block:
messages.btc.scan.firstHeightRequired: Enter the first block height to scan.
messages.btc.scan.noneFound: No unspent payments found in this range.
messages.btc.scan.singleProvider: Output and spent status were checked with the configured Esplora provider. This is a single-provider check, not independent verification. Select and review each exact transaction output below.
messages.btc.headers.heading: Block headers
messages.btc.headers.storageNote: Checked block headers are public chain data (no keys, addresses or payments). They are saved in this browser per network so the next check resumes, and checked again before use.
messages.btc.headers.verified: Block headers checked on this device from the pinned genesis block to height {height} (tip {hash}): linkage, proof of work, difficulty rules, timestamps, versions, and the most cumulative work among the headers the server sent. Every scanned block must be on this chain. This is not SPV and not full validation: the server can still hide a heavier chain, and proof of work is cheap on test networks.
messages.btc.headers.restored: Resumed from {count} saved block headers. All of them were checked again on this device before use.
messages.btc.headers.discarded: Saved block headers failed validation and were discarded. Headers are downloaded and checked again from the genesis block.
messages.btc.headers.lessWork: The server offered a competing chain with no more work than the headers already checked. It was ignored, and blocks from it are refused.
messages.btc.headers.reorg: A chain with more work replaced the checked headers above height {height}.
messages.btc.headers.resultsDropped: Scan results above height {height} came from blocks that are no longer on the checked chain and were removed ({count} payments). Scan those blocks again.
messages.btc.headers.scanDiscarded: The scanned blocks are no longer on the checked chain. The scan results were discarded; scan again.
messages.btc.headers.failed: Header check failed: {reason} Headers checked before the failure are kept. No scan runs until a header check succeeds.
messages.btc.headers.behind: Block headers are checked only to height {height}, below the first height to scan. Nothing was scanned.
messages.btc.headers.notSaved: Checked block headers could not be saved in this browser. They are downloaded and checked again from the genesis block next time.
messages.btc.headers.loading: Checking saved block headers again: height {height}…
messages.btc.headers.forget: Forget saved headers for this network

messages.policy.intro: A policy meta-address (scheme 0x47500002) makes every payment land in a small contract account that can only pay out to your chosen destination, after a delay and within per-token limits. A stolen key is delayed, not stopped: watch the account and cancel what you did not sign.

messages.policy.network.heading: Network and contracts

messages.policy.create.needSession: Load or generate seller keys first (Seller keys).
messages.policy.create.otherKeys: Record verified, but it belongs to other seller keys than the ones loaded now. Scanning will not find its payments.
messages.policy.create.badDestinations: Enter one or more checksummed destination addresses.
messages.policy.create.notFound: No match among these destinations, the delay presets and the known limits roots. A policy with limits can only be restored from its record.
messages.policy.create.restored: Policy found and restored. Download the record now.
messages.policy.create.destinationLabel: Destination (the only address withdrawals can go to)
messages.policy.create.destinationHint: Use a wallet you control and keep. Changing it later takes twice the delay and can be cancelled by anyone holding your keys.
messages.policy.create.limitsHint: Leave empty for no limits. With limits, a token without a row can never be withdrawn. Amounts are base units; window in seconds; token "native" for the coin.
messages.policy.create.keepBody: Without the record (destination, delay and limits) the account cannot be deployed and nothing can be withdrawn. It holds no keys, but it links your destination to this meta-address: store it privately, next to your seller key backup.
messages.policy.create.lostBody: The policy hash in a meta-address can be matched against likely destinations and the delay presets, locally. Policies with limits need their record.

messages.policy.pay.metaHint: Get it from the payee over a channel you trust: you cannot check the policy behind it.
messages.policy.pay.amountInvalid: Enter the amount as a whole number of base units.
messages.policy.pay.connectToSend: Connect a wallet on this network to send.

messages.policy.pay.lockedBody: Your wallet already sent a transaction for this payment, but it could not be verified. Keep the hashes below and check your wallet and a block explorer before doing anything else. Start over only after checking: an approval that was mined stays in effect, and a new review can use it.
messages.policy.pay.unlock: I checked my wallet: start over
messages.policy.pay.alreadyPaid: You already sent this exact payment (same payee, token and amount) from this tab: transaction {hash}. Check it in your wallet or a block explorer. To pay again on purpose, clear this payment under Wallet attempts first, and for a token payment also its approval.

messages.policy.account.notDeployed: Not deployed yet. Deploying reveals the full policy (destination, delay, limits) on-chain.

messages.sellerKeys.pairing.intro: This carries only public data: your meta-address, invoice-signing public key and chain ids. It holds no private key, but it is private to your devices: share it only with a device you own, then compare the keys on both screens. It is not authenticated.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.caption: Public seller config for pairing
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.importLabel: Scan or paste a public seller config
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.fileTooBig: That file is too large or unreadable for a public seller config.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.compare.same: These keys match the keys loaded on this device. Nothing was changed.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.compare.different: These keys differ from the keys loaded on this device. Nothing was changed. Confirm the owner through another channel before relying on them.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.compare.none: No keys are loaded here, so there is nothing to compare. Nothing was changed. Compare the values with the sending device's screen and confirm them out of band before you copy or share this meta-address.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.secrets.title: Moving secret keys is separate
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.secrets.body: This pairing never contains secrets. The encrypted keystore does contain your secret keys: it can only be exported or imported with the passphrase-encrypted backup and import on this page. Anyone who gets that file and passphrase can spend your funds.
messages.registry.exportHint: This QR holds only your public meta-address, the same value you may publish. Whoever scans it can pay you privately-addressed funds; it reveals no private key and does not publish anything.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.refused: That is not a supported public seller config. It was too large, the wrong kind or version, altered, or it contains invalid keys. Nothing was changed.
messages.sellerKeys.pairing.exportFailed: The public seller config could not be prepared from the keys loaded on this device, so it is not shown. Nothing was changed.
messages.backup.title: Backup checklist
messages.backup.intro: Two things need a copy outside this tab: your seller keys and your client tags. Each item shows what actually happened. Keys count as Done when a copy exists outside this tab (a downloaded keystore, imported keys or a saved vault). The tag archive counts as Done only after its file was produced and handed to your browser. Neither proves that you stored the copy somewhere safe.
messages.backup.keys.heading: Step 1: seller keys
messages.backup.keys.notStarted: No copy of these keys exists outside this tab yet. Download an encrypted keystore in the Back up (encrypted) section above, then return here.
messages.backup.keys.done: A copy of these keys exists outside this tab (a downloaded keystore, imported keys or a saved vault). Keep that copy and its passphrase safe: neither can be recovered.
messages.backup.tags.heading: Step 2: client tag archive
messages.backup.tags.notStarted: No tag archive was downloaded in this session yet. Use the form below.
messages.backup.tags.partial: Last tag archive downloaded {time}. Tags in it: {count, number}. Some scan history is NOT in it (see below). Tags saved, changed or deleted after that, here or in another tab, are not in it either.
messages.backup.tags.failed: The latest tag archive attempt failed and produced no file: {reason} An archive from an earlier attempt, if you made one, is not affected.

messages.create.passphrase.protect: Protect the entire invoice with a passphrase

messages.create.passphrase.hintSuggested: Suggested: {words} random words picked on this device ({bits} bits); type it again below, or replace it with your own (use several unrelated words).
messages.create.passphrase.hintSend: Send the passphrase to the payer through a different channel from the invoice link.
messages.create.matching.label: Register this invoice in my encrypted reconciliation vault for automatic local matching
messages.create.matching.hint: Off by default. Only the invoice digest, nonce, chain, token, expected amount and validity window are stored, encrypted on this device with your viewing key; line items and memo are not. Matching happens on this device only: nothing about the invoice is added to the payment or its announcement. You can remove registrations in the Scan view.
messages.create.result.title: Your invoice link
messages.create.bearer.title: Bearer link
messages.create.bearer.lead: Anyone who has this link or its QR code can pay it.
messages.create.bearer.passphrase: The invoice contents are protected by a passphrase, which you must send separately; the passphrase cannot be recovered if lost.
messages.create.bearer.encrypted: Anyone with the link can also read the invoice because its encryption key is inside the link.
messages.create.bearer.plain: Anyone with the link can read the invoice.
messages.create.bearer.copies: Phone photo backups, clipboards, chat previews and browser history may keep a copy. Do not post it publicly unless that is intended.
messages.create.registration.busy: Registering the invoice in your encrypted reconciliation vault…
messages.create.registration.ok: Invoice registered in your encrypted reconciliation vault for local matching.

messages.create.buffer.label: Gas buffer policy
messages.create.buffer.range: Accept gas buffers within a range
messages.create.buffer.hint: Payers may add a small native-coin buffer so the one-time address can be swept without a linked wallet; each buffer publicly links the payment, the address and the payer. Amounts are whole wei, digits only, the maximum must be at least the minimum, and the minimum may not exceed {capWei} wei ({capNative} native coin), because payers refuse larger buffers.
messages.create.buffer.v2Notice: A buffer policy makes this a v2 invoice, which lean builds of this app do not accept. Payers on a lean build cannot pay it. Leave this off unless your payers use the full app.
messages.create.buffer.error.min: Enter the minimum buffer as a whole number of wei from 1 to 2^256-1, digits only.
messages.create.buffer.error.max: Enter the maximum buffer as a whole number of wei from 1 to 2^256-1, digits only.
messages.create.buffer.error.order: The maximum buffer must be at least the minimum buffer.
messages.create.buffer.error.cap: The minimum buffer is above the {capNative} native coin safety cap that payers apply ({capWei} wei), so no payer could meet it. Enter a smaller minimum.
messages.create.buffer.nativeHint: Gas buffers only apply to token invoices. A native-coin invoice never carries a buffer policy, so it stays a standard invoice that lean builds can pay.
messages.scan.title: Scan and receive
messages.scan.needKeys: Load or generate seller keys first.
messages.scan.intro: Announcements are downloaded from your RPC and checked inside a dedicated worker. The worker gets public logs and your viewing key for this scan only; it cannot reach the network.
messages.scan.rpcPrivacy.title: RPC privacy
messages.scan.rpcPrivacy.body: Your RPC provider sees your IP address, scan ranges, and logs. Verifying a router payment also requests token transfer logs filtered for the one-time address, or the transaction receipt; these requests can reveal which public announcements matched your keys. A configured second provider sees the same verification evidence. Use trusted private RPC providers or your own nodes if this matters to you.
messages.scan.disclosure.summary: What each party learns with your scan privacy settings
messages.scan.disclosure.hint: Change the scan transport, windows and delays in Settings. None of these options hides anything on-chain.

messages.scan.startBlock.hint: The first block to scan from.
messages.scan.deepScan: Deep scan (also check wrong view tags)

messages.pay.scan.needsPassphrase: This invoice needs a passphrase. Its header is unverified until it opens.

messages.pay.receipt.intro: This checks the receipt signature against the current signed invoice, chain, asset and exact seller amount. If this page has a transaction hash or prepared one-time address, those are checked too. A seller signature proves control of a key and does not independently prove an on-chain payment or seller identity.
messages.pay.receipt.privacy: A receipt may reveal a private amount, transaction and invoice association on this screen.
messages.pay.receipt.consent: I consent to opening private receipt details on this screen.
messages.pay.receipt.keyHint: Use only a compressed public key you verified with the seller through another channel. Leave blank to require the receipt key to match the valid invoice-signing key.
messages.pay.receipt.scanLabel: Scan or paste a seller receipt

messages.pay.receipt.matchTrustedKey: The signature matches the explicitly trusted key you entered, and the invoice digest, chain, asset and seller amount match. This is a seller-key attestation, not independent payment proof.
messages.pay.public.title: What becomes public
messages.pay.public.body: Your address, the token, the amounts, the fee and the time are public on-chain. The seller’s identity is not revealed by the one-time address.
messages.pay.delay.label: Wait a random time first ({min} to {max} minutes)
messages.pay.delay.hint: Timing friction only, not anonymity. While waiting nothing is signed or sent, and the page must stay open. You can cancel or send now.

This publicly links your payment, the one-time address and the buffer. It is an estimate ({gas} gas{source, select, simulated {, from a simulated token transfer} other {, default table value until you prepare the payment}} at up to {fee} wei, +20 %), not a guarantee.{raised, select, yes { Raised to the seller's minimum buffer for this invoice.} other {}} It is never refunded.
messages.pay.waiting.notice: Scheduled locally. Nothing has been signed or broadcast.
messages.pay.noWallet: No browser wallet found. Install or unlock one, then reload this page.

messages.pay.status.unverified: Status: unverified. A transaction with this hash is in block {block}, but it was not compared with the preview, so this app does not report it as this payment.
messages.pay.receipt.download.confirm: This receipt contains the amount and time of your payment. Keep it private. Download?

messages.walletAttempts.heading: Wallet attempts in this tab
messages.walletAttempts.hint: Every attempt remains here, including ones that returned a hash or were confirmed, until you check your wallet and explicitly clear it. While one remains, the same action cannot be sent again from this tab. A returned hash does not prove payment. Clearing this record cannot cancel an in-flight wallet request or roll back a transaction. This journal belongs to this browser tab; it does not protect attempts in other tabs or devices.
messages.walletAttempts.unknown: Outcome unknown; check your wallet before retrying.
messages.walletAttempts.confirmClear: Have you checked the wallet and chain outcome? Clearing permits another attempt and may cause a duplicate payment. It cannot cancel or roll back an in-flight request. Clear this record?
messages.walletAttempts.clear: Clear this attempt after checking my wallet
messages.disclosure.fee.signed: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, whose signature was verified by a release key built into this app). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.unsigned: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, which is unsigned and permitted only as a testnet development manifest). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.fee.unavailable: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to {#mono}{recipient}{/mono} (shown from the deployment manifest, with signature status unavailable). Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.

messages.disclosure.fee.none: GhostPay charges {pct} % on payments made through its checkout contract. The fee goes to the address in the deployment manifest, but {chain} has none loaded: {#strong}payments disabled on this chain{/strong}. Paying the stealth address directly costs no GhostPay fee.
messages.disclosure.observer.1.learns: Payer address, token, gross and net amounts, the fee flow to the fee recipient, router use, the announcement (stealth address, ephemeral key, view tag), timing, and the sweep source and destination if swept in the clear.
messages.disclosure.observer.1.not: Seller identity from the stealth address alone; invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.2.learns: Client IP, user agent, which app files were fetched, timing.
messages.disclosure.observer.2.not: The URL fragment, keys, invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.3.learns: Client IP, queried block ranges and addresses, submitted transactions.
messages.disclosure.observer.3.not: Viewing or spending keys (never sent); invoice contents.
messages.disclosure.observer.4.learns: IP (hashed), the stealth address, destination, token, amount, fee, timing; can censor.
messages.disclosure.observer.6.learns: The entire invoice (it is a bearer link).
messages.disclosure.observer.7.not: Payer or seller identity beyond public chain data.
messages.disclosure.limit.1: GhostPay does not hide the payer, the amount, the token, the time, or the router call. It hides which seller owns the one-time (stealth) address.
messages.disclosure.limit.2: A sweep from a stealth address to a known wallet links them on-chain. Sweeping through a relayer does not remove that link.
messages.disclosure.limit.3: An invoice link is a bearer secret: anyone who has the link (or its QR code) can read it. The signature only shows the link was not altered by someone without the signing key; it does not prove who the seller is.
messages.disclosure.limit.4: The optional delay is timing friction, not anonymity: no cover transactions are created and the final transaction is public.
messages.disclosure.limit.5: The optional gas buffer is a public native transfer in the same transaction as your payment and links the payer to the stealth address.
messages.disclosure.limit.6: This app runs entirely in your browser, but your browser, extensions, wallet, RPC provider and operating system are all trusted by it. It has had no external audit.

messages.bill.linkTooLong: The invoice link is too long to print as a QR code. Share it digitally instead.
messages.bill.passphraseNote: This link is passphrase protected. The passphrase is not printed: give it to the payer separately.

messages.tagArchive.heading: Client tags: encrypted backup and key rotation
messages.tagArchive.loadKeys: Load seller keys to back up or restore client tags.
messages.tagArchive.passphrase.label: Archive passphrase (at least 14 characters)
messages.tagArchive.passphrase.suggested: Suggested: {words} random words picked on this device ({bits} bits). Write it down, then type it again below, or replace it with your own.
messages.tagArchive.format: Format: scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and AES-256-GCM, .gpa file with a fixed name that never contains labels. The archive holds your tags, not your keys. Anyone with the file can try passphrases offline, so use a strong one. The page you are using can read unlocked tags: a script injected into it could too, so keep this page free of untrusted extensions.
messages.tagArchive.import.summary: {total} tag(s) in the archive: {added} new, {updated} updated, {kept} kept because your copy is newer, {removed} local tag(s) removed.
messages.tagArchive.import.historyNote: Scan history for {count} chain(s) will be merged in separate transactions. A failure can leave a partial import. Restored observations remain history; they are not fresh payment proof.
messages.tagArchive.import.readOnly: This import makes the history vault read-only because its safety limit has been reached.
messages.tagArchive.rotate.heading: Rotate tag keys
messages.tagArchive.rotate.warning: This re-encrypts every tag under a new salt in one all-or-nothing step. It does not protect data exposed earlier and does not replace your viewing key: if the viewing key may be compromised, generate new seller keys instead.
messages.tagArchive.wipe.heading: Delete all tags
messages.tagArchive.wipe.warning: This deletes every tag in this browser. Download an archive first if you may need them.
messages.tagArchive.wipe.last: Last chance: this cannot be undone.
messages.tagArchive.msg.encrypting: Encrypting (this takes a moment on purpose)…
messages.tagArchive.msg.invalidArchive: This is not a valid GhostPay tag archive.
messages.tagArchive.msg.historyOpen: Scan history for chain {chain} cannot be opened here. No import was started.
messages.tagArchive.msg.decrypted: Archive decrypted. Review the summary; nothing has been changed yet.
messages.tagArchive.msg.interrupted: Import interrupted; subsequent stores were not started.
messages.tagArchive.msg.imported: Imported: {added} added, {updated} updated, {removed} removed. Tags committed.
messages.tagArchive.msg.importedHistory: Scan history committed for {count} chain(s); restored history remains historical evidence, not a fresh scan.
messages.tagArchive.msg.incomplete: Import incomplete. Tags: {tags}. {outcomes} {reason} Stores commit separately; inspect local data and make a new preview before retrying.
messages.tagArchive.msg.rotated: Tag keys rotated (key version {version}). Archives made earlier still open with their own passphrase. This does not replace your viewing key.
messages.tagArchive.msg.downloaded: Archive downloaded: {count} tag(s). SHA-256 {sha}. Keep the file and the passphrase: neither can be recovered.
messages.tagArchive.missing.skipped: Scan history for {count} chain(s) could not be read and is NOT in this archive.
messages.tagArchive.missing.unlisted: The scan history kept for chains this build does not support could not be listed; any such history is NOT in this archive.
messages.tagArchive.missing.unsupportedOne: Scan history stored in this browser for {chains} is NOT in this archive: this build does not support that chain.
messages.tagArchive.missing.unsupportedMany: Scan history stored in this browser for {chains} is NOT in this archive: this build does not support those chains.

messages.sol.title: Solana stealth payments (test networks)
messages.sol.warning.body: Unaudited. Mainnet is disabled. Use only coins that have no value (devnet, testnet or a local validator). Keys are held in memory and are never saved; write down the seed if you want to keep the wallet.
messages.sol.rpc.label: RPC server URL
messages.sol.rpc.hint: Any Solana JSON-RPC server you trust for this network (https, or http to localhost for a local validator). It sees the transactions you scan, each one-time address whose balance you check, and any transaction you broadcast. It cannot see your keys.
messages.sol.rpc.missing: Enter the RPC server URL (https, or http to localhost for a local validator).
messages.sol.instr.1: The payer needs a tool that supports GhostPay Solana stealth payments on {network}. This view does not send payments.
messages.sol.instr.2: The payer pastes the address above (or scans the QR code), derives a one-time address from it, and sends SOL to that address.
messages.sol.instr.3: The same transaction must carry the announcement memo ({#mono}gpst1:...{/mono}); without it this wallet cannot find the payment.
messages.sol.instr.4: Wait for finalization, then use "Scan" below starting a little before the payment slot.
messages.sol.qr.caption: Solana stealth payment request ({network})
messages.sol.slot.label: First slot
messages.sol.slot.hint: Scans finalized announcements from this slot up to the server head, at most {max} pages of 1000 transactions. Every transaction is downloaded and checked on this device.
messages.sol.slot.required: Enter the first slot to scan.
messages.sol.singleProvider: Payments and balances were checked with the configured RPC provider. This is a single-provider check, not independent verification. Select and review the exact one-time address below.
messages.sol.destination.hint: A {network} address. Check it carefully: a sent transaction cannot be reversed.
messages.sol.fee.hint: The fee is fixed at the base rate for one signature; this app has no fee oracle.
messages.tron.title: TRON stealth payments (test networks)
messages.tron.warning.body: Unaudited. Mainnet is disabled. Use only coins that have no value (Nile, Shasta or a local node). Keys are held in memory and are never saved; write down the key backup if you want to keep the wallet.
messages.tron.node.label: Node URL
messages.tron.node.hint: Any TRON full node or TronGrid-style HTTP API you trust for this network (https, or http to localhost). It sees the blocks you scan, each one-time address whose balance you check, and any transaction you broadcast. It cannot see your keys. This app only refuses a node that reports mainnet; it cannot prove which test network the node is on.
messages.tron.node.missing: Enter the node URL (https, or http to localhost for a local node).
messages.tron.appLocked: The app locked, so this wallet's keys were wiped from memory. Import the backup keys to use it again.
messages.tron.import.label: Or import keys
messages.tron.import.hint: 128 hex characters (64 bytes) from the backup of a wallet created here. Test coins only.
messages.tron.instr.1: The payer needs a tool that supports GhostPay TRON stealth payments on {network}. This view does not send payments.
messages.tron.instr.2: The payer pastes the address above (or scans the QR code), derives a one-time TRON address from it, and sends TRX to that address.
messages.tron.instr.3: The same transaction must carry the announcement memo ({#mono}GPT1{/mono}); without it this wallet cannot find the payment.
messages.tron.instr.4: Wait for the block to be produced, then use "Scan" below starting a little before it. TRC-20 tokens are detected but not swept here.
messages.tron.qr.caption: TRON stealth payment request ({network})
messages.tron.block.label: First block
messages.tron.block.hint: Scans at most {max} blocks per run up to the node head. Whole blocks are downloaded and checked on this device.
messages.tron.block.required: Enter the first block to scan.
messages.tron.tokens: {count} TRC-20 payment(s) not shown; this view sweeps TRX only.
messages.tron.singleProvider: Payments and balances were checked with the configured node. This is a single-provider check, not independent verification. Select and review the exact one-time address below.
messages.tron.destination.hint: A {network} address (T...). Check it carefully: a sent transaction cannot be reversed.
messages.tron.sameAddress: Choose a different address than the one-time address being swept.
messages.tron.fee.hint: The fee reserve is estimated from the node's chain parameters when you review.
messages.tron.signed.notSent: Not sent yet. Broadcasting sends it to the node above.
